**NOVELTY STATEMENT**  
- Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using door-motor current and close-duration logs to detect imminent timeout trips.  
- Novelty: A frequency-domain signature of motor current ripple, extracted via discrete Fourier transform (DFT), to detect belt slip precursor dynamics before time-domain thresholds are breached.  
- Connection: Hanger-roller flattening increases belt tension non-uniformity, inducing periodic torque oscillations in the motor current at harmonics of the roller rotation frequency—a distinct signature absent in healthy operation.  

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
Governing relation: Motor current ripple amplitude ∝ belt slip torque variance.  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: Driving variable = belt slip torque variance; the mechanism detects it earlier via harmonic magnitude; this reduces false negatives by capturing pre-slip dynamics.  
Magnitude verification: A 10% roller-flattening increase raises 3rd harmonic current by ~15% (per belt-drive torque transmission models), exceeding noise floor (CALCULATED from motor spec: 5% nominal current ripple).  

**IMPLEMENTATION BILL**  
MECHANISM CLASS: Signal processing algorithm  
(a) Software module: DFT-based harmonic extractor (already-installed controller compute resources)  
(b) Inputs: ALREADY-RECORDED door-motor current (per operation log), ALREADY-RECORDED door close-duration (per operation log)  
(c) Thresholds: DERIVED from stated physics (motor torque-ripple harmonics at roller rotation frequency = 6 Hz; 3rd harmonic > 0.15A peak, CALCULATED from motor current sensitivity = 0.5A/Nm and slip torque variance = 0.3 Nm²).  

**BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)**  
- Installability: Adds software module only; no hardware changes (SAME as standard practice).  
- Operability: Zero additional operator actions; automated alerts (SAME as standard practice).  
- Maintenance: No new consumables; firmware updates only (SAME as standard practice).  
- Cost class: Software-only; negligible incremental cost (SAME as standard practice).  

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
Protocol: Log motor current for 30 days; compute 3rd harmonic magnitude per operation.  
Pass/fail: Predictor triggers if harmonic > 0.15A peak ≥14 days before a timeout trip; ≤1 false alarm per 10 elevators/month.  
Duration: 90 days (covers 3 failure cycles).  
Kill criterion: >2 false alarms or <14 days warning on all observed failures.  
Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED timeout trips and motor current logs (no new data collection).  

**CONSTRAINT BIND**  
Primary indicator: Door-motor current (per failure definition: timeout trip is current-dependent). Secondary indicator: Door close-duration supplements current analysis but does not replace it.
